senses.definition: A short, soft, high-pitched sound, as made by a baby bird.
(chiefly in the negative) A feeble utterance or complaint.
examples: I don't want to hear a peep out of you!

senses.definition: The sound of a steam engine's whistle; typically shrill.

quotes.text: With a "peep" from a high-pitched whistle, the train would leave by the crossover to the down line, […].

quotes.text:
"Peep, peep," said Edward, "I'm ready."
"Peep, peep, peep," said Henry, "so am I."

senses.definition: (birdwatching, colloquial) A sandpiper or other small wader.

quotes.text: When I spotted two small warm-brown scaley-plumaged ‘peeps’ with yellow legs, my commentary immediately identified them as Least Sandpipers.
quotes.reference: 1983, Bill Oddie, Gone Birding, London: Methuen, page 91:

senses.definition: To make a soft, shrill noise like a baby bird.
To speak briefly with a quiet voice.
(intransitive) To look, especially through a narrow opening, or while trying not to be seen or noticed.
examples: The man peeped through the small hole.

quotes.text: And it was while all were passionately intent upon the pleasing and snake-like progress of their uncle that a young girl in furs, ascending the stairs two at a time, peeped perfunctorily into the nursery as she passed the hallway—and halted amazed.

quotes.text: But Richmond[…]appeared to lose himself in his own reflections. Some pickled crab, which he had not touched, had been removed with a damson pie; and his sister saw, peeping around the massive silver epergne that almost obscured him from her view, that he had eaten no more than a spoonful of that either.

senses.definition: (intransitive, dated) To begin to appear; to look forth from concealment; to make the first appearance.

quotes.text: When flowers first peeped, and trees did blossoms bear.
